children: ) declined to their lowest level in more than four months Monday as traders anticipated a U.S. government report showing increased global grain supplies.

Corn futures fell as much as 0.8% to $4.38 a bushel in Chicago, their lowest since July 1, before recovering some losses. The U.S. Department of Agriculture is scheduled to release its monthly supply and demand estimates Tuesday.

Analysts surveyed by Bloomberg News expect higher corn inventories in South America to offset a modest reduction in U.S. production forecasts. The USDA surprised traders in October by raising its estimate for American corn yields, triggering a sharp decline in prices.

For investors, the upcoming report could influence agricultural commodity prices, grain trading companies and fertilizer producers. Larger inventories would likely add pressure to corn prices, potentially reducing farmers' revenue and demand for agricultural inputs.
Speculative positioning has also turned bearish, with investment funds recently shifting to net short positions in corn futures amid seasonal selling pressure from the U.S. autumn harvest.

title: Corn prices fall to 4-mth low ahead of USDA supply report
